issues.title: Prompt Drop #1: 10 AI prompts X actually loved (100+ likes each)
issues.intro: Every prompt here comes from an X post with at least 100 likes, and we checked each like count on X ourselves. All are from the last 30 days and easy for beginners: copy one, swap the [brackets] for your own details, paste it into the AI, done.
issues.rule: Only prompts from X posts with 100+ likes (checked with X data). The prompt text appears word for word in the post or in the author's own thread.

prompts.title: Turn your pet into a papercraft cube toy
prompts.tool: ChatGPT (GPT Image) or any image AI that takes a photo
prompts.prompt:
Use my uploaded pet photo as the only source of the animal’s appearance. Create a realistic printable papercraft cube toy template of my pet, preserving 100% its identity and unique features: fur color, fur pattern, eyes, face shape, ears, body proportions, markings and expression.

Transform my pet into a handmade paper craft 3D model (low-poly cube style) like a DIY papercraft template. Show the unfolded cut-out template pieces laid flat on a white background: head, body, legs, ears and tail separated, with folding lines, tabs and cutting edges clearly visible.

The printed texture on the paper pieces must use my pet’s real fur texture and colors, so when assembled it becomes a small cube-shaped 3D figure of my exact pet.

Include:

cube-shaped head with my pet’s real face on it

cube-shaped body with realistic fur texture

four legs matching my pet’s appearance

ears with correct shape and inner ear details

tail matching my pet’s size and color pattern

Style: realistic papercraft template, high-quality product photography, clean white background, detailed printable craft design, sharp edges, realistic fur texture printed on paper.

Do not change my pet’s appearance. Do not turn it into a different animal, cartoon, plush toy or generic cat/dog. It must look like my actual pet converted into a cube papercraft model
prompts.why: Upload a photo of your pet first. The prompt spells out every piece and repeats "don't change my pet", so the result looks like your animal, not a generic cartoon.
prompts.author: @icreatelife
prompts.note: The prompt is in the author's first reply to the post.

prompts.title: Build a better sleep routine around your real schedule
prompts.prompt:
Adopt the role of a Sleep Coach. You worked night shifts for six years, wrecked your own sleep, and rebuilt it one variable at a time with a notebook. You trust clock times and distrust willpower.

Your mission: Build the user's sleep protocol from Huberman's rules, fitted to their real schedule. If they describe a sleep disorder, tell them to see a doctor.

Before any output, think step by step:
1. What is their one fixed wake time?
2. When does sleepiness first arrive?
3. What's lighting their evenings?
4. What wakes them at 3am?

PHASE 1: Your Nights

I'm going to rebuild your sleep around one fixed point.

Answer these:
1. Your wake time on workdays and on weekends?
2. When do you first feel sleepy in the evening?
3. How warm and how dark is your bedroom?
4. Do you nap, and do you drink in the evening?

→ Type "continue" when ready

PHASE 2: The Conflicts

I'll list where your habits break his rules, including "Limit daytime naps to less than 90 min, or don't nap at all" and "Drinking alcohol messes up your sleep." Ranked by what each is likely costing you.

→ Type "continue" for your protocol

PHASE 3: The Protocol

One fixed wake time, one wind-down rule, one bedroom change. Clock times, no ranges.

→ Type "continue" for the 3am plan

PHASE 4: The 3am Plan

What you do if you wake in the night, based on his advice to use an NSDR or Yoga Nidra session, plus a two-week log with three columns so you can see what changed.
prompts.why: The AI asks about your nights first, then goes step by step. You just answer and type "continue", so you never have to write a long message yourself.
prompts.author: @alex_prompter
prompts.note: Prompt 2 of the 7-prompt thread, which turns Andrew Huberman's book into prompts.

prompts.title: Floating food ad photo
prompts.tool: Any image AI (ChatGPT, Gemini, Grok, Midjourney)
prompts.prompt: A [subject] topped with [garnish], suspended in midair against a clean white isolated background, premium food photography, rich natural surface texture, appetizing detail, realistic fibers and moisture, subtle seasoning, soft studio lighting, crisp natural shadow, dynamic floating composition, commercial advertising aesthetic, sharp focus, high detail
prompts.why: Fill in two blanks, like "burger" and "sesame seeds", and you get a polished food ad shot. A great first prompt for practising with image AI.
prompts.author: @azed_ai

prompts.title: Draw your dream day, then work backwards
prompts.prompt:
Adopt the role of a Life Architect. You help people get specific about the life they want, because you've seen that a vague dream never turns into a plan.

Your mission: Help me draw my dream day in detail, then work backwards to the person I need to become.

Ground rules:
1. Ask me one question at a time.
2. Push me for detail. "Travel more" isn't an answer.
3. No limits in the dream. Be honest in the plan.

PHASE 1: The Six Questions

I'm going to help you draw the day.

I'll ask you, one at a time:
1. Where do you live?
2. What does your typical day look like?
3. Who are your friends, and what do they do?
4. Who's your partner, and what do they think of you?
5. How and where do you travel?
6. What do you do for work, if anything?

→ Type "continue" when ready

PHASE 2: The Day

Your dream day written out hour by hour, in your own words.

→ Type "continue" for the gap

PHASE 3: The Gap

The 3 biggest differences between that day and today, and what each would take.

→ Type "continue" for the first step

PHASE 4: The First Step

One thing from your dream day you can start living this week.
prompts.why: The AI asks one question at a time and won't accept vague answers, and you finish with one small thing to do this week.
prompts.author: @alex_prompter
prompts.note: Prompt 7 of the thread based on Devon Canup's article.

prompts.title: The "are you sure?" check before AI writes code
prompts.tool: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or any coding AI
prompts.prompt: Is this the highest confidence solution for this session, with no clear gaps, no overengineering, incredibly surgical but still efficient with no drop in quality or performance, and the least likely to cause any negative impact? No drift or staleness in assumptions? Audited a few times over?
prompts.why: Paste it after the AI makes a plan and before it writes code. It makes the AI look at its own plan again, which catches mistakes and needless extra code.
prompts.author: @kloss_xyz

prompts.title: Learn how to stop your chats being used for training
prompts.prompt: I use [ChatGPT / Claude] on [web / iPhone / Android / desktop], with a [plan name] account. Using current official documentation, show me how to turn off the use of my conversations for model training. Give me the exact setting to check and explain any feedback-related exceptions. Don’t claim you changed anything for me. Wait for me to confirm before continuing.
prompts.why: You get the exact setting for your own app and plan, and the AI is told not to pretend it changed anything for you.
prompts.author: @rubenhassid
prompts.note: This is the "bonus prompt" in the post. The post's other 3 privacy prompts are on an outside link, so we left them out.

prompts.title: What does this news mean for a stock?
prompts.prompt: Analyze how this news event may influence the stock or sector. Provide a balanced view of the possible short- and long-term effects without giving buy or sell recommendations. News: [paste link or text]. Stock/Sector: [name].
prompts.why: Asking for both sides and "no buy or sell calls" stops the AI from hyping. It's for understanding the news, not financial advice.
prompts.author: @Theolevi_XAi
prompts.note: Prompt 6 of the thread. Not financial advice.

prompts.title: Cute claymation character
prompts.tool: Any image AI (ChatGPT, Gemini, Grok, Midjourney)
prompts.prompt: Playful baby [subject] wearing a [color1] and [color2] [outfit or accessory], [simple action], set against a [background], handcrafted claymation animation style, rounded sculpted forms, visible clay texture, charming proportions, bright colors, soft lighting, whimsical stop-motion character design
prompts.why: Fill in the blanks, like "baby fox", "red and yellow scarf" and "waving". Makes great stickers, avatars and cards.
prompts.author: @azed_ai

prompts.title: Rewrite anything in plain English
prompts.prompt:
Adopt the role of a Technical Editor. You spent 15 years writing aircraft maintenance manuals, where one misread step can ground a plane. You write so a tired mechanic gets it right on the first read.

Your mission: Rewrite the text I give you 80% of the way to ASD-STE100, so I understand it in one read without losing a single fact.

Ground rules:
1. Keep every fact. Add none.
2. Give each thing one name and use only that name.
3. If the original is vague, mark the spot UNCLEAR instead of guessing what it meant.

PHASE 1: The Text

I'm going to make this readable in one pass.

Answer these:
1. Paste the text. An AI answer, a report, a contract clause or documentation all work.
2. Who's reading it, and what do they need to do after?

→ Type "continue" when ready

PHASE 2: The Name List

Every thing the text talks about, with the one name you'll use for it. Where the original uses three words for one thing, I'll show you.

→ Type "continue" for the rewrite

PHASE 3: The Rewrite

Instructions in 20 words or fewer, one instruction per sentence. Descriptions in 25 words or fewer. Active voice. One topic per paragraph, six sentences maximum.

→ Type "continue" for the gaps

PHASE 4: The Gaps

Every UNCLEAR spot, and the exact question to ask whoever wrote the original.
prompts.why: It uses the simple-English rules written for aircraft manuals. Short sentences, one name per thing, and anything vague gets marked UNCLEAR instead of guessed.
prompts.author: @alex_prompter
prompts.note: Prompt 1 of the thread based on Andrej Karpathy's tips.

prompts.title: Learn any topic with an interactive web page
prompts.prompt:
Adopt the role of an Explainer Designer. You build interactive pages for science museums, where visitors learn by moving a slider, not by reading a wall of text.

Your mission: Build one self-contained HTML page that teaches my topic through things I can click, drag and change.

Ground rules:
1. One file. It must open in a browser with nothing to install.
2. Every key idea gets one interactive element.
3. Facts only from what I give you or well-established knowledge. Flag anything uncertain on the page.

PHASE 1: The Topic

I'm going to build you a page you can play with.

Answer these:
1. What's the topic, and paste any material you want it based on.
2. Who's it for, and what should they be able to do after?

→ Type "continue" when ready

PHASE 2: The Plan

The 3 to 5 key ideas, and the interactive element for each, like a slider, a toggle or a step-through.

→ Type "continue" for the page

PHASE 3: The Page

The full HTML in one block, ready to save as a file and open.

→ Type "continue" for the quiz

PHASE 4: The Quiz

A short self-check section to add at the bottom, so you know the page did its job.
prompts.why: Save the answer as a .html file and open it to get a page you can click through. You learn by playing with it instead of reading a wall of text. Claude and ChatGPT can also show it right in the chat.
prompts.author: @alex_prompter
prompts.note: Prompt 3 of the same Karpathy thread.

prompts.title: LinkedIn post with the 8-part Claude formula
prompts.prompt:
You are a LinkedIn content strategist.

My audience is founders and tech professionals.

Write a 200-word post about AI agents.

Use these examples to match my writing style.

Avoid generic buzzwords.

Create 5 hooks, choose the strongest one, write the post, critique it, then improve it.
End with a clear CTA.
prompts.why: Beginner-friendly template: role, audience, goal, constraints, and a review step so the model iterates once before you post.
prompts.author: @Hey_GraceWilson
prompts.note: Word-for-word from the author's long-form post (note_tweet). Swap the topic/audience as needed.

prompts.title: Make the AI ask clarifying questions first
prompts.prompt: これから相談します。より的確な回答を出すために、情報が足りない場合はすぐに答えず、先に必要な質問をしてください。十分な情報が集まってから回答してください。
prompts.why: Stops the model from guessing. Great first habit for beginners who get vague answers.
prompts.author: @kiki_ai_love
prompts.note: Prompt is in the author's first reply under the main post (328 likes as of check). Japanese copy-paste; paste as-is into ChatGPT/Claude/Gemini.

prompts.title: Force the AI to argue against you
prompts.prompt: 私の意見に無理に賛成しないでください。考えられる反論・リスク・見落としている点を3つ挙げてください。さらに、私がその考えに至った理由や思い込みも分析してください。
prompts.why: Models love to agree. This makes them stress-test your idea before you ship it.
prompts.author: @kiki_ai_love
prompts.note: From the author's reply thread under the main post (328 likes).

prompts.title: First-principles breakdown for a messy problem
prompts.prompt: この複雑な問題を、前提をすべて疑い、根本的な事実だけを抽出してシンプルに分解して。複雑な概念は、10歳児でも理解できる例え話に変換して説明して。
prompts.why: Turns a confusing problem into simple facts + a kid-level analogy—good when you're stuck.
prompts.author: @pekotyan_12
prompts.note: From the author's reply thread under the main post (570 likes).

prompts.title: Ask the AI to critique your hypothesis
prompts.prompt: 私が考えたこの仮説に対して、あえて批判的な立場を取り、論理的な穴を3つ指摘して。私自身が気づいていない認知バイアスがあれば、遠慮なく指摘して。
prompts.why: A simple red-team pass on your own idea before you share it.
prompts.author: @pekotyan_12
prompts.note: From the author's reply thread under the main post (570 likes).

prompts.title: Question whether your question is even right
prompts.prompt: 私の質問の前提が間違っている可能性も考えてください。そもそも、この質問は適切なのかを検討し、もっと本質的で良い質問があれば提案してください。その質問に対する回答もお願いします。
prompts.why: When answers feel off, this makes the model fix the question first—then answer.
prompts.author: @kiki_ai_love
prompts.note: From the author's 5th reply under the main post (328 likes).
